en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty Fifth Chapter
The Discussion on the Knowledge of the Asekha: Is there knowledge of the asekha for one who is still in training (sekha)? Yes.

Does the one in training (sekha) know and see the state of the one beyond training (asekha), and having attained what is seen, known, and realized, does he dwell having entered upon it, dwelling having touched it with the body?
One should not say so... [etc.

...Is it not the case that the one in training does not know and does not see the state of the one beyond training, and does not dwell having attained what is unseen, unknown, and unrealized, nor dwells having touched it with the body?
“Yes.

“If it is true that a trainee (sekha) does not know and does not see the state of one beyond training (asekha-dhamma), and does not dwell having attained what is unseen, unknown, and unrealized, nor dwells having touched it with the body, then surely you should not say:
‘A trainee possesses the knowledge of one beyond training.’”

Is there, for one who is beyond training (asekha), knowledge that belongs to one beyond training; does one beyond training know and see the state of one beyond training; does he dwell having entered upon what is seen, known, realized, and attained; does he dwell having touched it with the body? Yes.

Is there, for one in training (sekha), knowledge that belongs to one beyond training; does one in training know and see the state of one beyond training; does he dwell having entered upon what is seen, known, realized, and attained; does he dwell having touched it with the body?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does the trainee possess the knowledge of one beyond training?

Yes. Does the trainee know and see the state of one beyond training? No. Does he dwell having failed to attain what is unseen, unknown, and unrealized, and failing to dwell having touched it with the body? Yes.

The one beyond training possesses the knowledge of one beyond training; yet the one beyond training does not know or see the state of one beyond training, does not dwell having attained what is unseen, unknown, and unrealized, and does not dwell having touched it with the body—is this not so?
One must certainly not say so … [and so on] … Does the one in training possess the knowledge of one beyond training?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Does a person who is a lineage-holder possess knowledge of the path of stream-entry?
[The respondent replies: “One should not say so …pe…”
Is there knowledge of the fruit of stream-entry for a person who has entered upon the way to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry?

One should not say so … [and so on] … Is there knowledge of the fruit of once-returning … of the fruit of non-returning … of Arhatship for a person who has entered upon the way to the realization of Arhatship? One should not say so.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“The knowledge of one beyond training exists in one who is still in training”?
“Yes, [he does].
“But surely the Venerable Ānanda is still a learner (sekha) who knows: ‘The Blessed One is sublime,’ and who knows: ‘The elder Sāriputta and the elder Mahāmoggallāna are sublime’?
“Yes, he does.”
If the Venerable Ānanda is still a trainee (sekha), yet he knows, “The Blessed One is sublime,” and he knows, “The Elder Sāriputta and the Elder Mahāmoggallāna are sublime,” then indeed, sir,
it must be said that a trainee possesses the knowledge of one who is beyond training (asekha). The Discussion on the Knowledge of One Beyond Training is finished.
